chunks: Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
If a slave had a bondwoman as his wife and he divorced her once, then both of them were freed, she would remain with him on the basis of one divorce.

key_terms.أَمَةٌ: a bondwoman or female slave; the wife in this case
key_terms.أُعْتِقَا: the two of them were manumitted and became free
key_terms.الْعَبْدُ: a male slave; the husband in this ruling
key_terms.عَلَى تَطْلِيقَةٍ: with one divorce still counted in legal effect

ai.seo_question: If a slave divorces his bondwoman wife once and then both are freed, does that divorce still count?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning divorce between a slave man and a bondwoman when both later become free. It states that a prior single divorce remains legally counted after emancipation, so their status continues on the basis of that one pronouncement.
